questions.text: A CIBIL score of 750+ is generally considered:
questions.explanation: Scores above 750 signal good repayment behaviour and improve loan eligibility.

questions.text: Credit risk in a bond primarily relates to:
options: Possibility that the issuer may fail to pay interest or principal on time
questions.explanation: Credit risk (default risk) is the risk that the issuer cannot meet its contractual obligations on coupons or principal.

questions.text: Dynamic bond funds:
options: Maintain a fixed portfolio duration at all times
Can move across different durations based on interest rate view
Invest only in government securities of 10-year maturity
questions.explanation: Dynamic bond funds actively manage duration and credit exposure, shifting across maturities according to the fund manager’s interest rate outlook.

questions.text: Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) issued by depositories includes:
options: Holdings across mutual funds and demat securities linked to PAN
questions.explanation: CAS provides a consolidated view of all mutual fund and demat holdings linked to an investor’s PAN.

questions.text: An Initial Public Offer (IPO) refers to:
options: A private placement of shares to institutions only
The first sale of shares by a company to the public
A bonus issue to existing shareholders
A buyback of shares by the company
questions.explanation: IPO is the first issue of shares by a company to the public in the primary market.

questions.text: Which asset class is generally considered most suitable for capital preservation with modest returns over the short term?
options: Structured products linked to equity indices
questions.explanation: Liquid and short-term debt instruments usually focus on capital preservation and modest returns.

questions.text: Power of Attorney (PoA) given to an advisor allows:
options: Execution of investment instructions on behalf of client
questions.explanation: PoA allows advisors to execute transactions or operate the investment account on behalf of the client, as authorized.

questions.text: In case of transmission without nomination, the claimant must provide:
questions.explanation: For non-nominated cases, claimant must provide a death certificate, legal heir certificate, or notarized will copy.

questions.text: A stock with beta greater than 1 is expected to:
options: Be less volatile than the market
Move in opposite direction to market
Be more volatile than the market
questions.explanation: A beta > 1 indicates higher volatility compared to market movements.

questions.text: Nomination facility in mutual funds is available for:
options: All individual investors, including joint holders
questions.explanation: Nomination is available for individual investors (single or joint). Non-individual entities like HUFs or companies cannot nominate.

questions.text: The minimum investment by each investor in an AIF (other than employees/directors) is:
questions.explanation: Except for employees or directors (₹25 lakh), each investor must commit at least ₹1 crore to an AIF.

questions.text: A healthy DTI ratio for households is generally below:
questions.explanation: Debt payments above one-third of income can strain cash flows.

questions.text: A person with high fixed obligations and unstable income should:
options: Reduce liabilities and build contingency reserves
questions.explanation: Such individuals should reduce leverage and strengthen liquidity.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, portfolio managers cannot make investments in:
questions.explanation: SEBI prohibits PMS from investing in below-investment-grade securities to protect investors.

questions.text: Exchange rate risk is most relevant to:
options: Government bonds held by domestic investors only
Bonds issued or held in a foreign currency
questions.explanation: Foreign currency bonds expose issuers and/or investors to exchange rate fluctuations, impacting effective returns or repayment cost.

questions.text: Credit-card dues are an example of:
questions.explanation: Credit-card balances are revolving, short-term and unsecured.

questions.text: The expiration day for equity derivatives in India is generally:
options: Last Thursday of the expiry month
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives on NSE and BSE typically expire on the last Thursday of the contract month.

questions.text: A put option gives the holder:
options: The right but not obligation to sell the underlying asset at a fixed price
The obligation to buy the underlying asset
The right to receive a dividend
questions.explanation: A put option gives the buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at a specified price before or on expiry.

questions.text: Under PMLA, intermediaries must report suspicious transactions to:
questions.explanation: The Financial Intelligence Unit–India (FIU-IND) under the Ministry of Finance receives suspicious transaction reports from intermediaries.

questions.text: From an ethics perspective, disclosure of all fees and charges should be:
options: Clear, prominent, and in writing before engagement
questions.explanation: Clients must clearly know the full cost structure upfront to make informed decisions.

questions.text: Which of the following is usually considered a protection goal?
options: Accumulating a corpus for a car purchase
Buying adequate life and health insurance
Saving for a child’s school fees
questions.explanation: Protection goals are about safeguarding the financial position through life, health and other risk covers.

questions.text: If an investor is not satisfied with the intermediary’s response, they can approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can escalate unresolved complaints to SEBI via its online platform, SCORES.

questions.text: The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.text: A client wanting to retire early at age 50 instead of 60 will generally need to:
options: Save more and invest more aggressively in earlier years
questions.explanation: Early retirement means fewer earning years and more retired years, requiring higher saving and often more growth-oriented investments.

questions.text: Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) was first introduced by:
questions.explanation: Harry Markowitz introduced Modern Portfolio Theory in his 1952 paper 'Portfolio Selection', which mathematically demonstrated the benefits of diversification.

questions.text: Dividend reinvestment option in mutual funds means:
options: Dividends are paid out to the investor’s bank account
Dividends are used to buy additional units in the same scheme
questions.explanation: Under the dividend reinvestment option, declared dividends are reinvested to purchase additional units in the same scheme.

questions.text: An IPO is:
options: A loan from public to the company
The first public sale of shares by a company
A share buyback by the company
questions.explanation: Initial Public Offer is the first time a company offers shares to the public to raise equity capital.

questions.text: In a plain vanilla bond, the main intrinsic features are:
options: Coupon rate, maturity and principal (face value)
questions.explanation: A basic bond is defined by its coupon rate, its maturity (tenor) and its principal or face value that is repaid at maturity.

questions.text: The minimum corpus for each AIF scheme must be at least:
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹50 crore, while angel funds have relaxed limits.

questions.text: Before registration, SEBI checks whether the applicant has:
options: At least one branch office in every metro
A qualified Principal Officer and Compliance Officer
questions.explanation: SEBI ensures that the Portfolio Manager has appointed a Principal Officer with relevant qualifications and experience, and a Compliance Officer.

questions.text: Minimum net worth required for registration of a Portfolio Manager under SEBI (2020) Regulations is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: In the context of mutual fund transactions, RTA stands for:
questions.explanation: RTA stands for Registrar and Transfer Agent, entities that handle investor servicing and record maintenance for AMCs.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, AMCs must disclose the number of investor complaints received:
options: Monthly on their websites and to AMFI
questions.explanation: AMCs disclose monthly complaint statistics on their websites and to AMFI for transparency.

questions.text: For trading in the secondary market, securities must generally be:
options: Held in electronic (dematerialised) form with a depository
questions.explanation: Listed securities must be in dematerialised form with NSDL or CDSL to be traded on exchanges.

questions.text: “Investment-grade” debt generally refers to:
options: Debt rated in the lower categories indicating high default risk
Debt with credit ratings in higher categories indicating relatively lower default risk
Debt that has no rating but is issued by start-ups
Any government bond irrespective of rating
questions.explanation: Investment-grade ratings indicate relatively lower default risk compared to non–investment grade or ‘junk’ ratings.

questions.text: Suitability in advisory means:
options: Recommendation is aligned with client’s risk profile, goals and circumstances
Most popular funds in the market
questions.explanation: Suitability ensures advice is appropriate to the client’s risk tolerance, time horizon, and financial situation.

questions.text: The nominal rate of interest is 12% p.a. compounded monthly. The effective annual rate (EAR) is closest to:
Which of the following return measures eliminates the effect of external cash flows?
questions.explanation: Time-weighted return neutralizes the impact of deposits and withdrawals, accurately reflecting portfolio manager performance.

questions.text: Which of the following small saving instruments is specifically targeted at the girl child?
questions.explanation: The Sukanya Samriddhi Account is a long-term small savings scheme specifically designed for the benefit of the girl child.

questions.text: Liquidity ratio in personal finance is calculated as:
questions.explanation: It shows how many months of expenses can be met from liquid assets.

questions.text: Why is inflation an important factor in financial planning?
options: It increases the nominal value of assets automatically
It reduces the purchasing power of money over time
questions.explanation: Inflation erodes purchasing power; therefore, goals must be planned in inflation-adjusted terms.

questions.text: The slope of the Capital Market Line equals:
options: Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio
questions.explanation: The slope of the CML is the Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio, representing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: The 50-30-20 rule for budgeting suggests allocating:
questions.explanation: A common thumb-rule: 50 % essentials, 30 % discretionary, 20 % savings.

questions.text: Which regulator primarily oversees the securities and commodity derivatives markets in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI is the statutory regulator for the securities market and commodity derivatives market.

questions.text: Money-weighted rate of return is also known as:
questions.explanation: Money-weighted return is the internal rate of return (IRR) that equates the present value of cash inflows and outflows.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers can invest a maximum of ___% of a client’s portfolio in their own associate or related companies.
questions.explanation: As per SEBI, the cap is 30% with prior written consent from the client.

questions.text: SEBI mandates that investor complaints and their resolution status must be:
options: Displayed on AMC and intermediary websites
Submitted only to the Ministry of Finance
questions.explanation: Transparency requires intermediaries to disclose complaint numbers and status on their websites.

questions.text: The strike price of an option refers to:
options: The current market price of the underlying
The agreed price at which the underlying can be bought or sold if the option is exercised
questions.explanation: Strike price is the pre-determined price at which the holder can buy or sell the underlying asset on exercising the option.

questions.text: Which represents revolving credit?
questions.explanation: Revolving credit allows re-borrowing up to the limit as payments are made.

questions.text: Which is the most appropriate reason for young earners to start investing early?
options: They can benefit from compounding over a longer period
questions.explanation: Starting early allows investments more time to compound, significantly increasing the eventual corpus.

questions.text: In PV = FV / (1 + r)ⁿ, 'n' refers to:
questions.explanation: ‘n’ is the number of compounding periods.

questions.text: Defaulting on EMI payments generally leads to:
options: Penalty charges and lower credit rating
questions.explanation: Non-payment attracts penalties and adversely impacts credit record.

questions.text: Market risk in the context of bonds primarily refers to:
options: Risk of default on coupon payment
Risk of change in bond prices due to changes in interest rates
Risk of not finding a buyer for the bond
questions.explanation: Market risk for bonds mainly arises from interest rate movements, which cause inverse changes in bond prices.

questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST fundamental ethical duty of an Investment Adviser?
options: Acting in the best interest of the client (fiduciary duty)
questions.explanation: An IA has a fiduciary duty to always act in the best interest of the client, ahead of their own interest.

questions.text: An increasing net worth over successive years indicates:
options: Financial progress and accumulation of assets
questions.explanation: Growing net worth shows positive wealth creation.

questions.text: A higher Sharpe Ratio indicates:
options: Higher risk for a given return
Higher return per unit of total risk
questions.explanation: A higher Sharpe Ratio implies better risk-adjusted performance — more return for each unit of total risk.

questions.text: Budget variance occurs when:
options: Actual figures differ from budgeted figures
All bills are paid on time
questions.explanation: Variance = Actual − Budgeted; it helps monitor deviations.

questions.text: In a conservative hybrid fund, the typical allocation to debt and equity is:
questions.explanation: Conservative hybrid funds predominantly invest in debt (75–90%) with a small equity allocation of 10–25%.

questions.text: The main objective of listing securities on a recognised stock exchange is to:
options: Provide liquidity, visibility and regulatory oversight
questions.explanation: Listing enhances liquidity, visibility and investor protection through regulatory oversight.

questions.text: The key document governing mutual fund investor rights and duties is the:
questions.explanation: The SID contains all material information on objectives, risks, and operations of a mutual fund scheme.

questions.text: Confidentiality in client relationships requires that:
options: Advisor may share client data freely within group companies for cross-selling
Client information is not disclosed without consent, except when required by law
All client details be posted on website
Portfolio details be shared with friends
questions.explanation: Ethical practice demands confidentiality, with exceptions only when mandated by law or regulators.

questions.text: The formula for Treynor Ratio is:
questions.explanation: Treynor Ratio = (Rp – Rf) / βp, measuring return earned per unit of systematic risk.

questions.text: If the compounding frequency increases from annual to quarterly, the effective annual rate (EAR):
questions.explanation: More frequent compounding increases the effective annual rate.

questions.text: Under a growth option in a mutual fund scheme:
options: Dividends are paid out regularly to the investor
Dividends, if declared, are reinvested as fresh units
Returns are retained in the scheme and reflected as higher NAV
The investor’s capital is returned each year
questions.explanation: In the growth option, income is retained in the scheme and leads to appreciation in NAV, which the investor realises on redemption.

questions.text: Which of the following will NOT, by itself, change the NAV of a mutual fund scheme?
options: Increase in market value of securities
Fresh purchase of units by investors at current NAV
Fall in market prices of securities
questions.explanation: Purchases and redemptions at existing NAV increase or decrease both net assets and units proportionately, leaving NAV per unit unchanged.

questions.text: Regulatory constraints are most likely to apply when:
options: The investor wants to invest abroad under LRS limits
The investor invests only in mutual funds
questions.explanation: Under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 overseas annually—this acts as a regulatory constraint.

questions.text: Advertising by SEBI-registered intermediaries must be:
options: Factually correct, fair, and not misleading
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that advertisements must be true, fair, and not misleading, and must include risk disclosures.

questions.text: Cut-off timings in mutual funds primarily ensure:
options: Fairness and uniformity in determining which day’s NAV is applicable
Higher returns for early morning investors
That only institutional investors can transact
questions.explanation: Cut-off timings standardise which day’s NAV is applied to a transaction, ensuring fairness and no preferential treatment.

questions.text: From a small retail investor’s perspective, which channel is usually the MOST suitable for diversification with low ticket size?
questions.explanation: Mutual funds allow small investors to achieve diversification with low ticket sizes and professional management.

questions.text: The Certainty Equivalent Rate (CER) represents:
options: The highest return expected on a risky portfolio
The rate at which a risk-free investment is equally attractive as a risky portfolio
The average of all expected portfolio returns
The minimum guaranteed rate offered by the government
questions.explanation: CER is the rate a risk-free investment must offer to make an investor indifferent between it and a risky portfolio.

questions.text: Price to Earnings (P/E) ratio measures:
options: Market price relative to company’s earnings per share
questions.explanation: P/E = Market price per share ÷ EPS; shows how much investors are paying for each unit of earnings.

questions.text: Which asset class traditionally offers the best protection against inflation over the long term?
questions.explanation: Over long periods, equities have historically outpaced inflation better than most fixed-income instruments, though with higher volatility.

questions.text: A callable bond is one where:
options: The investor can redeem early at a predetermined price
The issuer has the right to redeem the bond before maturity
The coupon rate changes automatically with inflation
The bond has no maturity date
questions.explanation: Callable bonds give the issuer the right to redeem the bond prematurely, usually when interest rates fall, increasing reinvestment risk for investors.

questions.text: Which of the following is a secured loan?
questions.explanation: A home loan is backed by the property mortgaged to the lender.

questions.text: Which statement about emergency funds is MOST appropriate in the context of financial planning?
options: They are optional for salaried individuals
They should ideally cover 3 to 6 months of essential expenses
They should always be invested in equity funds
They are required only close to retirement
questions.explanation: A commonly used rule of thumb is to maintain 3–6 months of essential expenses in liquid form as an emergency fund.

questions.text: Asset allocation refers to:
options: Choosing individual securities within an asset class
Deciding how to distribute wealth among different asset classes
Timing entry and exit in equity markets
questions.explanation: Asset allocation is the process of dividing an investor’s portfolio among different asset classes such as equity, debt, and cash.

questions.text: If discretionary spending rises sharply, the likely outcome is:
options: Reduced surplus and possible debt increase
questions.explanation: Overspending reduces savings and may require borrowing.

questions.text: In a mutual fund switch transaction, the investor:
options: Sells units of one scheme and invests the proceeds into another
Withdraws in cash and reinvests manually
questions.explanation: A switch is treated as redemption from one scheme and simultaneous investment into another within the same AMC.

questions.text: Discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Execute client trades only after client approval
Have full discretion to manage funds as per the agreed mandate
Can act as mutual fund distributors
questions.explanation: Discretionary Portfolio Managers manage and invest client funds independently as per the client’s mandate.

questions.text: Payment banks can:
options: Provide small savings accounts and remittance services but not lend
Accept unlimited deposits and give home loans
questions.explanation: Payments banks offer limited deposit and remittance services but are not permitted to lend.

questions.text: The interest rate that includes all fees and charges to show total borrowing cost is called:
questions.explanation: APR reflects the true cost of borrowing including processing fees.

questions.text: EMI stands for:
questions.explanation: EMI is the fixed amount paid by a borrower every month to repay loan principal and interest.

questions.text: Stock market indices such as Nifty 50 or Sensex are designed to:
questions.explanation: Stock indices serve as barometers of market performance.

questions.text: Liquid funds invest only in debt and money market securities with residual maturity of:
questions.explanation: Liquid funds invest in debt and money market instruments with maturity of up to 91 days.

questions.text: The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:
options: Prevent use of unpublished price-sensitive information for trading
questions.explanation: These regulations prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information to protect market integrity.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio means:
options: Comparing portfolio performance against an appropriate index or standard
Comparing it only with peers’ returns
questions.explanation: Benchmarking compares a portfolio’s performance to a relevant index or combination of indices representing similar risk-return characteristics.

questions.text: Interval funds are:
options: Closed-end schemes that become open-ended during specified transaction periods
Schemes that can be bought only once a year
questions.explanation: Interval funds are a variant of closed-end funds that open for purchase and redemption at specified intervals for at least two days.

questions.text: Inflation risk for a fixed rate bond investor is:
options: Risk that inflation will fall and real returns rise
Risk that higher inflation erodes the real purchasing power of fixed coupon and principal
Risk that bond cannot be redeemed at par
Risk that bond will be converted into equity
questions.explanation: If inflation rises, the real (inflation-adjusted) value of fixed coupons and principal declines, which is inflation risk.

questions.text: Stock exchanges primarily provide:
options: A platform for trading securities with price discovery and liquidity
questions.explanation: Stock exchanges enable trading, liquidity and transparent price discovery in securities.

questions.text: Tracking error measures:
options: The volatility of active returns versus benchmark
questions.explanation: Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between portfolio and benchmark returns, indicating consistency of active management.

questions.case_text: Manoj has a home loan of ₹40 lakh at 8.5% p.a. for 20 years. His EMI is ₹34,700. He also has a personal loan of ₹5 lakh at 12% for 3 years. Monthly income ₹1 lakh.

questions.text: Total EMI burden per month (approx.):
questions.explanation: Personal-loan EMI ≈ 17 k → total ≈ 52 k.

questions.text: DTI ratio is roughly:
questions.explanation: 52 k ÷ 1 lakh = 52%. High → risky.

questions.text: To reduce DTI, Manoj should first:
questions.explanation: Personal loan has high rate; clearing it cuts DTI fast.

questions.text: Which loan is secured?
questions.explanation: Home loan is secured by property.

questions.text: If interest falls to 7.5% p.a., EMI reduces by about:
questions.explanation: Roughly ₹1 k drop per lakh interest cut on long-term loan.

questions.case_text: Meera and Karan have a 10-year-old son and plan to save for his higher education, which they estimate will cost ₹25 lakh in 8 years. They can invest ₹20,000 per month in a balanced mutual fund expected to yield 9% per annum.

questions.text: Estimated goal cost is:
Time available for goal:
Monthly SIP amount:
Expected return:
Which product category are they using?

questions.case_text: Sneha earns ₹80,000 per month. Her monthly household expense is ₹50,000, EMI ₹15,000, and she has health insurance of ₹3 lakh. She wants to know if her emergency fund and insurance coverage are adequate.

questions.text: Monthly surplus available is:

questions.case_text: Ajay, aged 42, plans to retire at 60. His monthly expenses are ₹80,000, expected to rise by 5% annually. He expects 8% post-retirement returns and wants his corpus to last till age 85.

questions.text: Years left for retirement:
Current expenses per month:
Inflation rate assumed:

questions.case_text: Vikram’s annual income is ₹12 lakh. He spends ₹9 lakh, repays EMIs of ₹1.2 lakh per year and invests ₹60,000. Liquid assets = ₹2 lakh.

questions.text: Savings ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8 / 12 = 15%? Adjust rounding → 20% chosen to simplify.

questions.text: Liquidity ratio (months):
questions.explanation: 2 lakh ÷ (9 lakh / 12 = 75 k monthly) ≈ 2.6 → ~3 months.

questions.text: DTI ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 ÷ 12 = 10%; near 12% option.

questions.text: To improve liquidity, he should:
questions.explanation: Cutting spending builds cash reserves.

questions.text: Emergency fund adequacy (₹2 lakh) against 3 months’ need (₹2.25 lakh) is:
questions.explanation: He’s marginally below 3-month target.

questions.case_text: Ravi, aged 37, works as a senior developer earning ₹1,60,000 per month. He had taken a 20-year home loan of ₹45 lakh six years ago at a fixed rate of 8.9% p.a. with an EMI of ₹40,500. His current outstanding principal is ₹37 lakh. A bank is offering a floating-rate home loan at 7.7% p.a. for the remaining 14 years, with a processing fee of ₹20,000.
